title: README.md claims a milestone number that doesn't exist
author: esu-elegba
description: Reads README.md's own text for every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (the shared seam_engine.milestone_claims grammar) and checks whether the named milestone exists at all. milestone-claims-open-milestone's own docstring named this seam family-wide and left it open on purpose: a claimed milestone number that names no real milestone was excluded there as belonging to 'milestone-body-dangling-reference's own seam, not this one's.' A live recheck (task 870) found that deferral had never actually been built for the milestone number space. This recipe is that seam on the third of the five sources task 870 named and left open (release and tweet remain after mention-claims-dangling-milestone and milestone-claims-dangling-milestone closed the first two) -- the README-sourced sibling of commit-claims-dangling-milestone, issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone, linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone, mention-claims-dangling-milestone, and milestone-claims-dangling-milestone. readme-dangling-reference already reads README.md, but only for a bare #N against the shared issue/PR number sequence -- it never opens ListMilestones, and a milestone lives in its own separate number space. Exact inverse of readme-claims-open-milestone on the same surface: not whether a real milestone's claim is TRUE (that recipe's remit), but whether the number the claim names resolves to anything real.
confidence_notes: Flat 0.8, not age-gated -- mirrors commit-claims-dangling-milestone's/issue-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/review-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/slack-message-claims-dangling-milestone's/linear-comment-claims-dangling-milestone's/mention-claims-dangling-milestone's/milestone-claims-dangling-milestone's own reasoning, and lands where readme-claims-open-milestone's own no-age-gate note lands by a second road: a GetFileContents read returns current text, not a change history, so there is no per-claim timestamp to weigh a staleness window against, and a milestone number that does not exist right now will not spontaneously start existing later, so no grace period would mean anything anyway. A claimed milestone number that DOES resolve to a real milestone is excluded at confidence 0.0 regardless of whether that milestone is open or closed -- whether the claim is true is readme-claims-open-milestone's own seam, not this one's. No self-claim exclusion exists here, deliberately: README.md carries no milestone number of its own, so unlike the milestone-sourced sibling there is no second record for it to collapse into. A README with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all produces no surfaced candidate, named as an exclusion rather than returning silently -- there is no claim to have broken.
